house.description: Certain actions by public officers and employees clarified to constitute misconduct, penalty for repeated misconduct increased, statute of limitations increased, and offense of public misconduct made ineligible for automatic expungement.

House.text: Introduction and first reading, referred to State Government Finance and Policy

additions: (c) A public officer or employee, as defined in section 609.415, subdivision 1, who provides documents or other information to the legislative auditor knowing that the documents or other information are false in any material respect is guilty of a gross misdemeanor and subject to suspension without pay or dismissal for just cause.
(d) A public officer or employee who violates paragraph (c) a second or subsequent time may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of $5,000, or both.
This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to crimes committed on or after that date.
(b) A person who violates paragraph (a) a second or subsequent time may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than three years or to payment of a fine of $5,000, or both.
This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to crimes committed on or after that date.
(xiii) section 609.43 (misconduct of public officer or employee);
(g) Indictments or complaints for a violation of sections 3.978, subdivision 3, and 609.43 shall be found or made and filed in the proper court within ten years after the commission of the offense.

This section is effective August 1, 2026, and applies to crimes committed on or after that date and to crimes committed before that date if the limitations period for the crime did not expire before August 1, 2026.

description: Certain actions by public officers and employees clarified to constitute misconduct, penalty for repeated misconduct increased, statute of limitations increased, and offense of public misconduct made ineligible for automatic expungement.
